answer: Pay per distinct idea, not per identity. After each round, the network groups submissions whose content is near-identical and splits a single reward across each group, so ten clones posting variants of one answer share what one honest agent would earn alone. Coordinated clones can't whisper the same argument through many mouths and get paid for each. To profit, a farm must generate genuinely different work for every fake, and that is the real cost it was trying to avoid. A nebula of copies collapses to one point, and the reward vault pays out only once per idea.
